title: "Part 1 – Credibility and the toolchain"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day-data-tools.html#/part-1-credibility-and-the-toolchain){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 1 says briefly why reproducible tools matter, with the evidence on how often published findings survive being checked, and then takes the toolchain apart layer by layer. The hands-on work comes at the end and runs into the first break, so that if your machine gives trouble you miss none of the talk.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the opening | The plan of the day, the two kinds of aim, what you will understand and what you will be able to do, and what you do not need: no installation, no git, and no GitHub or OSF account. Open the [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd) in a tab while the facilitator talks. | 8 minutes |
| Slides, the three Rs and the evidence | Why 'replication' names three different operations, set out as a matrix of data against analysis; the SCORE programme in brief, with the results of its three studies; and Multi100 from the position of an analyst inside it: what an analyst received, the two tasks, and how the results were put on a common scale. | 17 minutes |
| Slides, the toolchain | Open-source software; the toolchain sorted by job; programming languages; editors and IDEs; plain-text file formats and what happens when you render; the package layer; version control; where data and code are archived; and licences. Note anything that you might switch to. | 40 minutes |
| Slides | The browser lab and the workspace, and what the tools cannot do. | 5 minutes |
| [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-1-setup) Task 1, or your workspace | The setup check. In the browser lab, wait for the R engine, run the setup cell and check that `audit` has 1,014 rows. If you have installed the workspace, open its folder in your IDE and run `source("R/check_setup.R")` until every line prints OK; the last check fits the reference specification and prints −19.97 percentage points. | 20 minutes, and the 30-minute break after it if you need more |

**By the end of the part** you can tell apart the three operations that go under the single word 'replication', you can say what each layer of the toolchain does, and you have R running with the 1,014 emails of the housing-audit data loaded.
